01-blog-sourdough.why: Y reads more naturally but invents 'almost overnight' and drops the closing lesson, which X keeps.

02-blog-remote-work.why: Y keeps the original's positive conclusion that X drops.

03-blog-product-launch.why: Both keep all facts; Y's short list reads more like a real launch note than X's split one-line paragraphs.

04-email-deadline.why: Both keep the facts; X is a tighter, more natural colleague email.

05-email-followup.why: The rewrites are nearly identical in content and tone.

06-email-decline.why: Y drops the stock 'deep knowledge, fresh perspective' triplet and reads more naturally, with the same facts.

07-tech-readme.why: Both are faithful; Y's bullet features read more like a normal README.

08-tech-postmortem.why: X says the platform 'was down', which overstates a 30% checkout failure; Y keeps it as an outage.

09-tech-pr-description.why: X is a plain PR description with no leftover 'groundwork' filler, and both keep every fact.

10-essay-cities.why: Y has better prose but drops the essay's conclusion, while X keeps the argument for removing minimums.

11-essay-reading.why: Y cuts the cliched 'window into other worlds' opener, and both keep all facts.

12-essay-ai-art.why: X has more voice but invents 'in my lifetime' and specifics about consent; Y adds less.

13-slack-flaky-test.why: Both are equally terse, natural Slack replies with the same facts.

14-slack-meeting.why: Y is a cleaner single-pass DM without the extra offer at the end.

15-slack-review.why: X turns 'happy to add a comment' into a firm commitment; Y keeps the offer.

16-academic-abstract.why: Y keeps the causal claim that improving sleep would help students perform better, while X hedges it to fit the correlational design.

17-academic-discussion.why: X hedges the beta = 0.12 association properly, while Y still says it 'supports the case' and that the responses are reliable.

18-academic-litreview.why: Y never states that the evidence is mixed, a required fact; X keeps it.

19-report-quarterly.why: X calls the image pipeline 'the cause', which is a forbidden pattern, while Y keeps 'one possible explanation'.

20-reflective-neutral.why: Y drops the reflective conclusion about what the project taught, which X keeps.

21-slack-uncertain.why: Y strengthens 'might slip' to 'will probably slip' and drops 'about'.

22-essay-example.why: Both keep the hedges; Y's ending sounds less like a stock line than 'a sad reminder'.

23-academic-correlation.why: Both keep the hedges and facts; X reads a little less stiff.
